text: Why does `repaint()` post a request rather than drawing immediately?
choices: So painting can be moved to a background thread when the loop is busy.
So the toolkit can compute which region became dirty before painting it.
So several changes in quick succession produce one redraw, and so all drawing stays on the event dispatch thread.
So the component can be validated and laid out before its contents are drawn.
explanation: Coalescing is the first reason and thread confinement the second, and both matter. It also explains the constraints on `paintComponent`: it must be able to run at any time, must be fast because it is on the loop, and must be idempotent, since the number of calls is not yours to know.
